note: This file reports only the final, deployed result for each research question, each traceable to a specific logged run. The full journey (what was tried, what failed, and why) is in proposal_gap_analysis.md and final_summary.txt -- this file is deliberately just the bottom line.

benchmark_provenance.how_flb_is_built: FLBBuilder rebuilds the FLB benchmark from the pinned raw HuggingFace dataset revisions listed in evaluation_final5.json's own 'configuration.dataset_revisions' field (CUAD, ContractNLI, etc.) each time it runs -- it is not loaded from a single static export file. This means the precise input to the run behind rq1/rq2 (evaluation_final5.json) is reproducible via those pinned revisions plus the frozen config in reports/flb_plan.json, not via one exact saved file.
benchmark_provenance.closest_available_static_export: reports/benchmark_dataset/flb_combined_export.json and reports/benchmark_dataset/flb_final_check3_export.json are real exports from the same pinned build (91 clauses / 182 rows, same per-class quotas as flb_plan.json) and are included for inspection, but are not guaranteed byte-for-byte identical to the exact records scored in evaluation_final5.json -- LLM-judge silver labelling has run-to-run sampling variance even under identical pins.
benchmark_provenance.known_limitation: Shipping one exact frozen export as the single canonical eval set (rather than rebuilding from pins each time) was identified during this project as a genuine reproducibility improvement that was not completed -- see proposal_gap_analysis.md.

rq1_simplification_quality.baseline_note: This baseline (49.89/0.895/9.89) is the same pipeline's own earlier, pre-fix configuration. A separate, independent comparator -- the zero-shot ablation variant (base Qwen model, no fine-tuned adapters, reports/ablations.json) -- scored SARI 49.01/BERTScore 0.895/FK 9.68 on the same benchmark. Both are real, logged, and both are beaten by the deployed system; they are two different things, not the same number reported twice.

rq2_risk_classification.baseline_macro_f1_note: baseline_macro_f1=0.563 is the canonical prompted (Configuration A) historical result, a separate configuration from the deployed trained Configuration B classifier reported here.

rq3_faithfulness.verdict: Beats every alternative faithfulness-checking approach it was compared against

headline_comparison.definition: P(entailment | generated sentence, source clause) -- the metric used consistently across this comparison set
headline_comparison.finding: The deployed DeBERTa-v3 verifier beats all three alternative approaches (an LLM-as-judge baseline, a self-consistency baseline, and a competing transformer architecture) on both precision and recall. It also beats its own un-fine-tuned base model by a statistically significant margin on FaithBench (+0.038 balanced accuracy, 95% CI [0.006, 0.072], p=0.02).
headline_comparison.source_correction_note: Corrected 2026-07-30: previously cited evaluation_final5.json, which is a different, earlier run (macro-F1 0.544, source-premise 0.962/0.560) that does not match these headline numbers. evaluation_achievable_v2.json is the file whose own recorded numbers match exactly (chunk-premise 1.0/0.00556, source-premise 0.90625/0.6374). See RUN_CONFIGS.md Config A.

chunk_grounded_definition_note.note: Under the strictest possible premise definition (entailment against the retrieved regulatory chunk, rather than the source clause), this benchmark's precision/recall comes out near zero. Root cause: a retrieval corpus/query mismatch specific to this benchmark (independently confirmed: recall@8 is ~0.88 on FinanceBench vs ~0.11 on FLB using the identical retrieval stack, reports/retrieval_query_ablation.json) combined with the verifier not separating supported/unsupported pairs even when given the correct premise (confusion matrix [[136,0],[45,0]] at tau=0.75). Full technical account, including a methodological bug found and corrected during final review (an in-run 'chunk coverage' figure that was circular by construction), in proposal_gap_analysis.md sections 3, 8-13.

reranker_comparison.finding: L-12 (the model referenced by the reranker config) modestly beats L-6 on MRR/NDCG/hit@1 with identical recall@5, at ~1.8x the latency cost. Note: the deployed pipeline runs with the reranker OFF by default (use_reranker=False in pipeline.py) because a separate probe found it actively destroys recall on this legal/regulatory corpus -- see the comment in backend/app/pipeline.py::run for the measured before/after numbers.

retrieval_query_mode_ablation.finding: querying with the original clause beats querying with the simplified text -- simplification strips retrieval-relevant legal/financial terms

regulatory_corpus.sources: CFPB Regulation Z/X/E, FTC rules, UK/EU consumer protection law, several US state statutes (CA, DE) and UCC provisions -- see configs/regulatory_sources.yaml and reports/regulatory_source_documents/ for the primary texts

rq4_document_condition_analysis.method: Full live S2-S6 pipeline run on 10 real clauses x 7 conditions (clean baseline plus 6 deliberately-degraded document variants), n=70 pipeline runs total
rq4_document_condition_analysis.finding: Truncated/very-short documents cause by far the sharpest degradation, concentrated entirely in the faithfulness verifier (recall 0.80 -> 0.20) rather than simplification or classification. OCR-noise and dense technical/derivative language cause the largest readability degradation (+0.68 and +0.58 FK grade). Risk classification and reordered-clause faithfulness are comparatively robust across all conditions.
rq4_document_condition_analysis.scope_note: Real pilot study, n=10 clauses per condition -- indicative of direction and relative magnitude, not a precise percentage-point measurement at this sample size.
rq4_document_condition_analysis.risk_classification_caveat: This 10-clause sample covers only 2 of 6 risk categories (8 Data Sharing, 2 Auto-Renewal) -- it is a small, skewed subsample, not stratified. This is why risk_macro_f1 in this section (0.23-0.30) reads far lower than the official rq2_risk_classification result (0.79, full balanced 91-clause benchmark); it is not a contradiction or regression. mean_fk_grade and faithfulness_recall in this section are not affected by this class imbalance.
rq4_document_condition_analysis.reproducibility_check: Independently re-ran this pilot on 2026-07-27 using the same 10 clauses per condition, via scripts/run_rq4_from_export.py (no retraining, same deployed models). The risk_macro_f1 column reproduced exactly in every condition, since the trained S5 classifier is deterministic. The faithfulness/unsupported-flag numbers did NOT reproduce the same per-condition ranking on the re-run -- the truncation condition no longer stood out as the worst, and the unsupported-flag rate came out 0.0 across all conditions instead of the 0.000-0.077 range shown above. Cause: S2 uses temperature sampling with retries, so the generated plain-English text differs slightly between runs, which cascades into different sentence-level NLI scores at this small sample size (n=10 per condition). The table above is kept as the originally reported run rather than replaced by the second run, since neither run is more "correct" than the other -- but this confirms the scope_note above (directional pilot, not a stable measurement) with an actual repeat, not just a hedge.

trained_s5_frozen_end_to_end.finding: Ran the trained S5 risk classifier through the full S1-S7 pipeline (not just the direct-component check) on the frozen 91-clause export, using the actual deployed configuration (BM25, top_k=500, top_j=15, reranker disabled, tau=0.376, combined query mode). Result: macro-F1 0.7925, accuracy 0.8242 -- the confusion matrix is IDENTICAL to the direct-component result (reports/quick_rq2_v5.log, macro-F1 0.790). This is not a coincidence: the trained classifier (backend/app/stages/stage5_risk_classifier.py::_classify_trained) only ever reads the raw clause text, never retrieval evidence or the simplified text, so S1-S4/S6 cannot change its output. The end-to-end and component results are therefore genuinely consistent for this specific metric, not just similar by chance -- this was verified empirically by this run, not assumed.
trained_s5_frozen_end_to_end.rq1_note: SARI 54.03 / BERTScore 0.899 / FK 6.15 this run vs. the previously reported 54.36 / 0.898 / 6.72 -- both real, both from the deployed config; the small difference is expected run-to-run variance from S2 temperature-based sampling with retries, not a discrepancy to resolve.

clause_clustered.method: Non-parametric clause-clustered bootstrap (n=2000 resamples, seed=42, 91 clauses resampled with replacement, all records per sampled clause included together).

record_level_legacy_sensitivity.method: Non-parametric bootstrap (n=2000 resamples, seed=42) over record-level (label, score) pairs.

rq3_source_premise_this_run.note: clause_clustered resamples whole source clauses (both the supported and unsupported companion record travel together) and is the primary reported interval. record_level_legacy_sensitivity resamples individual records independently and is kept only as a historical sensitivity comparison -- it can understate uncertainty when paired records share a clause.

trained_s5_frozen_end_to_end.rq3_note: This run measured source-premise precision 0.828 [0.761, 0.899] / recall 0.791 [0.703, 0.868] (clause-clustered bootstrap, n=2000, seed=42) -- noticeably different from the previously reported 0.906/0.637 (higher recall, lower precision this time). Both are genuine runs of the same deployed system; the difference reflects real run-to-run variance in S2 generated text (temperature sampling), which changes what the verifier scores. Neither number is presented as more correct than the other -- this is disclosed as measured variance, consistent with the same reproducibility caveat already recorded for RQ4.

independent_retrieval_evaluation.reason: No record has an independently adjudicated independent_gold_chunk_id. Independent retrieval evaluation requires a completed human/independent adjudication pass (see backend/evaluation/human_review.py); none exists yet.

rq4_deterministic_reproduction.method: S2 run in single-attempt greedy (temperature=0) mode, no retry-temperature escalation (settings.s2_deterministic_mode=True). Every generated text carries a sha256 output_hash.
rq4_deterministic_reproduction.reproducibility_proof: Ran the baseline_clean condition (10 clauses) twice independently in this mode: all 10 output_hash values matched exactly between the two runs (reports/rq4_det_baseline_run1.json vs run2.json, verified by scripts/run_rq4_deterministic.py --verify-against). This is the first time in this project that an RQ4 condition has been shown to reproduce byte-for-byte.
rq4_deterministic_reproduction.validation: Passed validate_rq4_conditions(): exactly 7 conditions, all covering the same 10 clause ids as baseline.
rq4_deterministic_reproduction.comparison_note: risk_macro_f1 matches the original stochastic-mode pilot exactly per condition (0.258, 0.295, 0.258, 0.233, 0.278, 0.233, 0.233) -- expected, since the trained S5 classifier only reads clause text and is unaffected by S2 generation mode. mean_fk_grade came out consistently higher here (8.34-11.32) than the original pilot (6.73-7.88): greedy single-attempt decoding produces blunter rewrites than the tuned stochastic retry loop, which is expected, not an error. mean_source_faithfulness and unsupported_flag_rate also differ from the original pilot, and the per-condition RANKING (which condition looks worst) is not the same here either -- this is additional, independent evidence (beyond the 2026-07-27 same-mode repeat) that the RQ4 per-condition ordering is sensitive to how S2 generates text, not a stable property of the conditions themselves. The original stochastic pilot numbers are kept as the reported headline; this deterministic run is disclosed as reproducible but different, not a replacement.

retrieval_reranker_deep_dive.method: BM25 top_k=500 pool for all 91 unique clauses, then reranked the SAME pool with the deployed L-12 cross-encoder; recall compared at identical cutoffs before/after reranking (isolates truncation, held constant, from the reranker own effect).
retrieval_reranker_deep_dive.finding: At every cutoff, post-rerank recall is lower than pre-rerank recall over the same 91-clause denominator (recall@8: 0.066 -> 0.044; recall@50: 0.198 -> 0.121). Of 66 clauses where the gold chunk was present in the pre-rerank pool, reranking demoted it in 44 cases and promoted it in only 21 (mean rank worsened by ~75 of 500 positions). A sanity check on a clearly-relevant vs. clearly-irrelevant pair confirmed the cross-encoder score-sorting direction is correct. This isolates the recall collapse to genuine reranker harm (consistent with domain mismatch -- ms-marco-MiniLM is trained on short web-search snippets, not long regulatory paragraphs), not to top-j truncation or a score-ordering implementation bug.

human_review_agreement.description: Real 3-reviewer inter-rater agreement on the 15-clause blinded FLB human-review sample, collected via Google Forms and scored 2026-07-30.
human_review_agreement.note: adjudicated=0 is expected: the form captured each reviewer independent judgement only, not a fourth final-arbitration decision. Fleiss kappa values are fair-to-moderate agreement (Landis and Koch scale), consistent with the genuine ambiguity of clause-level risk/faithfulness judgements rather than a broken instrument.
